findings.evidence: Surjectivity.lean:139-143 `rw [← natCard_lowerRamificationGroup_zero K L, h0, Subgroup.card_bot] … rw [psiNat_of_isUnramified]; exact map_normUnits_unitFiltration K L v` is reproduced at 193-198 with `h0` replaced by `Subgroup.eq_bot_of_subsingleton (lowerRamificationGroup K L 0)`.
findings.fix: Extract the general statement once, e.g. `private theorem map_normUnits_unitFiltration_psiNat_eq_of_lowerRamificationGroup_zero_eq_bot (h0 : lowerRamificationGroup K L 0 = ⊥) (v : ℕ) : (unitFiltration L (psiNat K L v)).map (Algebra.normUnits K) = unitFiltration K v`, and call it from both branches (the subsingleton branch supplying `Subgroup.eq_bot_of_subsingleton _`). Note it needs no primality hypothesis.
findings.issue: The unramified case of norm surjectivity is proved twice: lines 138-143 (under `lowerRamificationGroup K L 0 = ⊥`) and lines 192-198 (under `Subsingleton (L ≃ₐ[K] L)`, which is the strictly weaker special case, since it gives `G_0 = ⊥` via `Subgroup.eq_bot_of_subsingleton`). Both derive `ramificationIndex K L = 1`, then `isUnramified_iff_ramificationIndex_eq_one`, then `psiNat_of_isUnramified` + `map_normUnits_unitFiltration`.

findings.evidence: Herbrand.lean:134-149 and Surjectivity.lean:199-214 are character-for-character identical apart from `NormShift`/`NormSurj`; Herbrand.lean:153-163 and Surjectivity.lean:218-228 likewise.
findings.fix: Prove the induction principle once (e.g. in `FiniteExtension/IntermediateField.lean` or a shared `Norm` helper): `private theorem of_finrank_prime_of_trans (P : ∀ (F : Type v) [Field F] [ValuativeRel F] [TopologicalSpace F] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField F] [Algebra F L] [ValuativeExtension F L] [Module.Finite F L] [IsGalois F L], Prop) (hprime : …) (htrans : …) : P K`, and obtain `NormShift`, `NormSurj` (and the Hasse–Arf descent) as instances.
findings.issue: `normSurj_of_forall_finrank_lt` (186-214) and `normSurj_of_finrank_le` (218-228) are a verbatim copy of the existing `normShift_of_forall_finrank_lt` (Norm/Herbrand.lean:121-149) and `normShift_of_finrank_le` (Herbrand.lean:153-163) with `NormShift` renamed to `NormSurj`: same `Group.IsSolvable.exists_normal_index_prime`, same `fixedField` instance plumbing, same `hF`/`hlt` nlinarith, same `d`-induction. The general content — a property of finite Galois extensions of local fields that holds in prime degree and is transitive along Galois towers holds for all of them — is now proved twice, and `HasseArfBelow`/`hasseArfBelow` in the new CyclicPGroup.lean is a third instance of the same descent.

findings.evidence: CyclicPGroup.lean:263-265 `have hdrop := (upperJump_iff K L u).1 hu ⟨(u : ℝ) + 1, …⟩ …; exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim _ _) hdrop.ne` vs CyclicReduction.lean:148-151 `have hdrop := (upperJump_iff K F u).1 hF …; exact hdrop.ne (Subsingleton.elim _ _)`. `grep` over Herbrand/Jump.lean shows no such lemma.
findings.fix: Add `theorem UpperJump.nontrivial {u} (hu : UpperJump K L u) : Nontrivial (L ≃ₐ[K] L)` (or `not_upperJump_of_subsingleton`) in `Herbrand/Jump.lean` next to `upperJump_iff`, and use it at both sites.
findings.issue: Lines 261-265 re-derive inline the general fact that a trivial Galois group has no upper break; the same four-line argument already sits inline at CyclicReduction.lean:146-151. The statement is fully general (no cyclic/p-group hypothesis) and belongs as a named lemma.

summary: Statements and hypotheses sit at the natural level, but the PR proves the same facts twice: the unramified norm-surjectivity branch appears in both new helpers in Surjectivity.lean, and the whole Galois-tower degree induction is copied verbatim from Norm/Herbrand.lean rather than factored into one induction principle.
